questions.q: Find out the major products from the following reactions.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution: Hydroboration–oxidation is an anti-Markovnikov reaction, with the hydroxyl group attaching to the less-substituted carbon. In an oxymercuration–demercuration reaction, an alkene is treated with mercury(II) acetate, and the product is treated with sodium borohydride. The net result is a Markovnikov addition product in which the $OH$ group bonds to the more substituted carbon atom of the alkene.

questions.q:
Given below are two statements :
Statement (I) : The boiling points of alcohols and phenols increase with increase in the number of C-atoms.
Statement (II) : The boiling points of alcohols and phenols are higher in comparison to other class of compounds such as ethers, haloalkanes.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
Statement I is correct as boiling point of alcohol phenols increase with increase in the number of C -atoms due to increase in van der Waals forces.
Statement II is correct, since alcohols phenols have intermolecular H -bonding therefore their boiling points are higher in comparison to other class of compounds such as ethers, haloalkanes.

Test Inference
$( a )$ $Dil . HCl$ Insoluble
$( b )$ $NaOHsolution$ Soluble
$( c )$ $B{r}_{2} / water$ Decolourization
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
(i) Aromatic compounds having $+ M$ group can decolourise bromine water.
(ii) Since the compound is insoluble in $HCl$, it shows that the compound is acidic.
(iii) As the compound is soluble in NaOH, this again shows that the compound is acidic.
The above three conclusions indicate that the compound is aromatic having $+ M$ group and acidic.
Hence, the answer is a phenol as it is aromatic and slightly acidic.

questions.solution:
Carbolic acid or phenol reacts with phthalic anhydride in presence of conc. ${H}_{2}{SO}_{4}$& to form phenolphthalein which is used as an acid base indicator. The phenolphthalein is colourless below pH 8.5 and attains a pink to deep red hue above pH 9.0.

questions.q: Salicylaldehyde is synthesized from phenol, when reacted with
options: ${CO}_{2}, NaOH$
${CCl}_{4}, NaOH$
${HCCl}_{3}, NaOH$
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
Salicylaldehyde is prepared by heating phenol and chloroform together in the presence of potassium hydroxide or sodium hydroxide. This reaction is called the Reimer-Tiemann reaction.

The Reimer Tiemann reaction is an organic chemical reaction where phenol is converted into an ortho hydroxy benzaldehyde using chloroform, a base, and an acid workup. This reaction can also be described as the chemical reaction used for the ortho-formylation of phenols.
